Resolves #18969

A region's last column now shows a closed right edge in its header and cells whenever unused width follows it. Wherever two regions meet, there is exactly one divider, in the header as well as the cells. CSS-only: two stylesheets, no JavaScript, no width model.

- **The trailing edge sits just outside the last column's box.** Cells use a `box-shadow`, because `::after` already carries the modified-cell marker. The header uses `::after`, because header hover uses `box-shadow`. Each region's own clip decides when the edge shows: a row's `contain: strict` and a header toolbar's `overflow-x: hidden` hide it wherever the column reaches the region's end, whether flush or scrolled to the end, and nothing hides it across unused width. The identity is the existing logical one: `neo-last-column` from `grid.Row` for cells, and the toolbar's last button for the header (header buttons are not pooled).
- **The header draws the seams its cells draw.** On `dev` the header had no divider at either seam, pixel-measured at a flush width: the start|center seam and the center|end seam both read header background. The locked start's last button now closes on its right, and the locked end's first button opens on its left, exactly where the cells' borders are.

Why no JS "spare width" flag: the model's `containerWidth − start − end` is 2px off the real clip here, because it includes the grid's own borders. That is exactly the band where a flag-driven inside border would double the #9623 seam. The clip is pixel-exact by construction, and it re-decides on every resize, column resize, lock change and scroll.

Evidence: L3 (headless Chromium pixel reads of the rendered grids in the CI-run component tier, plus light/dark goldens in the local visual tier) → L3 required (a paint contract: a box-shadow and a pseudo-element are invisible to every DOM read).

## Deltas from ticket

- **Header seams, added.** They were missing on `dev` in every layout, and without them the exposed-edge golden would show City's closed header edge beside an open Note header edge over closed Note cells. This is two rules in the stylesheet this PR already changes. It does not touch the spare header area's fill (D#18971).
- **Header seams follow the lock a column was built with.** A column's runtime `locked` change never reaches its header button's `neo-locked-*` class. For example, City locked to the start lands in the start toolbar without `neo-locked-start`, so that seam's header divider is missing while its cells keep theirs. The cells follow the runtime lock because `grid.Row` recomputes their classes on every render. This predates the PR and is separate from it: #18986, a one-line engine fix (mine, next).
- **The spare header area** keeps its fill, per the ticket's out-of-scope line (D#18971).

## Test Evidence

- **Red-first:** with the two stylesheets at `origin/dev` and themes rebuilt, 7 of the 8 arms fail, each at its own assertion. The three edge arms fail at the edge pixels, and the start seam and the three meeting arms fail at the header seam pixel. The flex control passes on both trees.
- **Mutations**, each killed by exactly its own arms (re-run at this head):
  - no cell `box-shadow` → the three edge arms (the cell pixels);
  - no header `::after` → the three edge arms (one pixel: the header);
  - the plausible wrong fix, dropping the `neo-last-column` rule so the last column keeps an inside border → seven arms: the three edge arms, and all four meeting arms at *no cell draws a second divider*. The start-seam arm stays green, since that rule never touches its seam.
- **Suites at this head (`5b13d5c953`, on dev `28fab65852`):** `component/grid` 56 passed; the e2e specs that load the changed fixture (`e2e/grid/CellEditing*`, `GridViewFocusOutline`, `KeyboardNavigationScroll`, `LockedRegionEmpties`) 125 passed; the spec 16/16 at `--repeat-each=2`. At the previous head: component tier 388 passed, `e2e/grid` 126 passed.
- **Visual tier:** `PreviewLanguageVisual` › the light pair fails 528 pixels on its own golden, identically with this PR's stylesheets reverted. It captures the dock preview board, not a grid.
